plan: [ Single second-price auction with two opponents and no history. With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value: it maximizes expected profit and avoids winning when the price exceeds your valuation. Overbidding risks negative payoff if the second-highest bid is above 20; underbidding risks losing profitable wins when second-highest is below 20. Therefore, bid exactly my value. ]

In a 3-bidder independent private values second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. There’s no prior history to exploit, and others’ values are uniformly drawn and independent each round. By bidding my value ($35), I win exactly when my value is highest and pay the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Tie-breaking is random; bidding above or below my value can only reduce expected payoff. Therefore, bid exactly 35.

[ In a 3-bidder, independent private values, second-price auction, the dominant strategy is truthful bidding. With no informative history (round 1 of 1), I should bid my value: 40. Overbidding risks paying above value if the second-highest exceeds 40; underbidding risks losing positive-profit wins. With 0.1 tick size and random tie-breaking, 40 is appropriate. ]
